record.excerpt: The 8 day and 21 day EMAs cross. … Wait for the cross, then monitor for a maximum of 6 days. … Set stop loss just the other side of the 21 day EMA and adjust daily. … If price crosses the 21 day EMA , your setup has failed. … You can see that the above rules produced much more profit than loss. … 6 positions were taken in 10 months (304 days), an average of one every 51 days.
record.performance_claim: produced much more profit than loss
record.notes: 8/21 EMA cross on BTC daily with stop at 21 EMA; qualitative backtest result over 304 days.

spec.claim_summary: Enter when the 8-day EMA crosses the 21-day EMA and exit if price crosses the 21-day EMA or after 6 days.

claimed.other: produced much more profit than loss

assumptions: Asset not named in claim text; BTCUSDT chosen as most natural reading because the page is about BTC.
Timeframe 1d chosen because the claim uses 8 day and 21 day EMAs and the page chart timeframe is 1d.
Direction set to long as closest testable core; the claim states a generic cross with no long/short qualifier.
Entry assumed on the close of the cross bar (fill next open); monitor for a maximum of 6 days interpreted as maximum holding period of 6 bars.
Exit uses close crosses_below 21-day EMA to represent the failure condition price crosses the 21 day EMA on the long side.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: trailing stop-loss just the other side of the 21 day EMA and adjust daily cannot be expressed as a fixed stop_loss_pct; approximated by exit on close below the 21-day EMA with no fixed stop.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: claim implies bidirectional trading with generic EMA cross covering both crosses_above for longs and crosses_below for shorts with symmetric stop on the other side of the 21-day EMA, but the schema allows only a single direction; this spec tests the long side only and short-side entries are not tested.

issues.problem: Claim says 'The 8 day and 21 day EMAs cross' with no long-only qualifier and symmetric stop/failure language. Spec restricts to long only and omits the short side, which changes trade set and verdict.
Missing short entry leg: 8-day EMA crosses_below 21-day EMA. Spec encodes only crosses_above, so bearish crosses implied by generic cross rule are never traded.
Missing short-side failure exit for shorts: price crosses the 21-day EMA from below. Spec encodes only long-side close crosses_below 21-day EMA.

report.headline: Tested an approximation of the claim. Makes money (+0.91% per trade after costs, 72 trades) but can't be told from luck: random timing did as well 28% of the time.
reasons: makes money after costs (+0.91% per trade), but random timing did as well 28% of the time (p = 0.285); needs p < 0.05 to count as an edge
warnings: just holding did better: +60% vs buy-and-hold +1781%
